full_results: kept with the work, not in this package (the full file exceeds the package file limit)
units: Callgrind Ir per call. A call is one loop iteration that calls a noinline wrapper around the primitive (bl, ret, argument set-up and wrapper prologue included); the 16 Ir of the empty loop (counter, dump request, sink update) are subtracted. Inlined use in the kernel is cheaper by those few Ir.

key_notes.x_max: branch-bounded maximum: every data-dependent branch inside the primitive replaced by a branch-free routine that costs at least as much, remaining control variants forced; includes the Fermat-chain fallback of blst_fp_inverse (133,370 Ir) executed unconditionally
key_notes.x_max_ct: as x_max but blst_fp_inverse costed as its constant-time half only, which is the path every tested input takes (3.4 million inputs, no fallback); not a proven bound if the fallback were reachable
key_notes.x_max_real_observed: largest value seen in the kernel's own code over the forced variants (all take the ct inversion)

method: step.c is included unmodified into harness.c (main renamed); the primitives measured are its own static functions.

A real wrapper (wr_*) and a bounded wrapper (wb_*) exist for every primitive; the bounded one has the control structure of the kernel's but every data-dependent branch inside the primitives replaced by a branch-free routine of at least equal cost.

Each variant's N inputs are built before the loop; the loop holds only the wrapper call, a counter and a Callgrind dump request; the Ir of each call is one dump (collection on throughout), less the 16 Ir of an empty loop.
N = 1000 and 2000 calls per variant; bound variants are constant (min = max) and equal for both N.
Equality of every bounded routine with the kernel's: at least 250,000 random/edge cases each (run on two builds); the check is shown to detect four injected faults.
The Fermat-chain fallback of blst_fp_inverse cannot be forced by any input found; x_max includes it, x_max_ct does not.

control_overhead.what_was_measured: rare_2cycle and rare_anchor of step.c, compiled in step.c's own unit (rare_anchor is instruction for instruction the shipped code, rare_2cycle has the same instructions in another order; see code_identity), on cycles of real curve points built with the kernel's own tables: 2-cycle (L=2) and long cycles L = 2, 3, 10, 33, 65. A copy of their control flow with noinline wrapper calls, a dump between every call, separates the control code from the primitives. The control code includes esc_seen (the diagnostic ring) in its dearest state: ring full, no match.
control_overhead.control_code_does: copies of 96-byte points into cyc[] (cyc[0] = *nw, cyc[len++] = s) and of the two cycle members in rare_2cycle, the loop counter and the len <= MAX_CYCLE test, flag tests (*dp, !esc), counter increments (two_cycles, long_cycles), stores of *sel, *kl, *dp, and the argument set-up of each primitive call
control_overhead.relation: shipped code (exact) <= wrapped copy for every scenario; the wrapped copy adds call overhead for each primitive

code_identity.meaning: In ship_driver.c's unit rare_anchor, new_trail, dp_restart, batch_step, add_single, key_full and canon_k_exact are instruction-for-instruction identical to step.c compiled alone (batch_step has three trailing alignment nops); rare_2cycle has the same 582 instructions in a different order (the shipped object holds a constant-propagated clone), so the end-to-end figure for rare_anchor is for the shipped code and the one for rare_2cycle for equivalent code. In harness.c's unit rare_2cycle, rare_anchor, batch_step, add_single (3 fewer instructions), key_full (register choice) and canon_k_exact (4 fewer) are compiled differently, so the per-primitive figures are for that unit's code

unmeasured_or_approximate: Per-primitive figures are for the harness unit's compile of step.c's functions, not the shipped object: add_single, canon_k_exact and rare_* are compiled differently there (inlining, 3 and 4 fewer instructions in add_single and canon_k_exact). The bounded figures exceed the harness code's by 6 to 7,000+ Ir (components >= 6), which covers differences of this size; it is not a proof.

Each primitive figure includes the call into and return from a noinline wrapper and the argument set-up (about 8-10 Ir); inlined use in the kernel costs that much less (the shipped rare_anchor with L = 65 is 3,135 Ir below the wrapped copy).

Control overhead of rare_2cycle/rare_anchor is measured on the wrapped copy (code between primitive calls: struct copies of cyc[], loop control, flag tests, counters) and on cycle lengths 2..65; paths not taken in the scenario (look-ahead DP break, cycle longer than 65 without escape, false-alarm exits) are cheaper than the escape path and were not run.

Dumps are cut at the dump request; the 16 Ir of the empty loop are an upper estimate of the harness's own cost per call (subtracted once); one Ir in 1000 of the empty loop reads 19, not 16 (not seen in primitive runs).
The Fermat-chain fallback of blst_fp_inverse was never taken (3.4 million inputs); its cost is measured (133,370 Ir) but it is not shown unreachable.

libc bcmp is the ifunc variant chosen under this Valgrind; a CPU feature set that selects another variant could change feq's real cost (the padded bound exceeds the dearest measured path, over all positions and alignments, by 10 Ir).
